unit.name: Decomposing deep research into pipeline stages
unit.description: The lecture moves from an end-to-end wake-word model to a multi-stage LLM system and shows why pipeline decomposition changes how engineers reason about failure and prioritization.
unit.summary: The second case study shifts to a deep-research assistant that answers broad queries by combining several steps rather than a single model [ts=3470s] [ts=3537s]. A baseline pipeline is sketched as query to LLM-generated search terms, then web search, then page selection/fetching, and finally LLM-based writing [ts=3603s] [ts=3680s]. The instructor notes that newer systems are more agentic and can decide to loop back for more search, but the simple linear version is already enough to expose the core project-management challenge [ts=3696s] [ts=3734s]. Once a system is decomposed this way, the key question is no longer only how to improve a model, but which pipeline stage deserves attention first [ts=3750s] [ts=3870s].

key_points.text: Many practical AI systems are pipelines rather than single end-to-end models.
A simple deep-research pipeline can be modeled as query generation, search, fetch, and writing stages.
Modern agentic variants add loops that decide when to gather more evidence.
The central engineering decision is choosing which pipeline component to optimize next.

kp_catalog.name: Pipeline decomposition for AI systems
kp_catalog.description: Representing an AI product as sequential components whose intermediate outputs can be inspected and improved independently.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Pipeline decomposition supports bottleneck diagnosis and error analysis.

kp_catalog.name: Manual error analysis to locate system bottlenecks
kp_catalog.description: A disciplined process of inspecting failing examples stage by stage and quantifying which subsystem accounts for most user-visible errors.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Manual error analysis is the lecture’s main reusable decision procedure for AI project strategy.
